journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Building Resilient Library Professionals: AI as a Catalyst for Emotional and Academic Skill Enhancement in School Libraries
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming library services across educational institutions, including academic universities and K-12 school libraries. This research explores how AI can catalyze the development of emotional intelligence (EI) and academic competencies among library professionals. The study examines AI technologies -including sentiment analysis, personalized learning platforms, virtual simulation training, and data analytics -alongside emotional intelligence dimensions encompassing empathy, self-regulation, and interpersonal skills. Through an integrated review of literature, case studies, and frameworks, this research demonstrates how library professionals can leverage AI to enhance professional resilience, adaptability, and service quality while addressing critical ethical considerations, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, and equitable access. Findings indicate that when thoughtfully implemented, AI and EI work synergistically to create more adaptable, empathetic, and practical library professionals.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Inclusive Education and Community Integration: Pathways to Empowerment and Social Participation of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
abstract: This research investigates the relationship between inclusive educational practices, community integration initiatives and long-term empowerment outcomes for individuals with intellectual disabilities. Through analysis of thirty-five educational and social integration variables across four comparison groups, the study identifies critical success factors in achieving sustainable inclusion. Findings demonstrate that effective inclusion requires coordinated efforts across institutional, familial and community domains rather than merely educational policy implementation. When individuals with intellectual disabilities receive support through well-designed inclusive settings, evidence-based instructional practices and consistent community assistance, they demonstrate notable progress in academic learning, social development, vocational readiness and quality-of-life outcomes. This study contributes to contemporary understanding of inclusive education as a comprehensive social transformation process and provides empirical support for policy reforms prioritizing equity, accessibility and universal design principles.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: The Pâninian Code: Sanskrit’s Renaissance in Digital Technology
abstract: Sanskrit, far from being a relic of antiquity, emerges as a sophisticated linguistic framework whose structural properties align remarkably with contemporary computational requirements. This paper investigates how a language perfected approximately 2,500 years ago now stands at the forefront of artificial intelligence research, neuroscience applications, and digital humanities initiatives. The study traces Sanskrit’s evolution through three distinct historical phases while examining its defining characteristics: rule-based grammatical construction, systematic phonetic organization, and an extensive manuscript corpus. Through analysis of governmental programs, technological implementations, and emerging interdisciplinary research, this work demonstrates how ancient linguistic engineering principles translate into modern computational utility. The research proposes a Three Pillars framework connecting classical Sanskrit properties to contemporary applications in AI, cognitive science, and knowledge preservation.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Education: A Comprehensive Analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative forces of the 21st century, reshaping industries and fundamentally changing how individuals interact with technology. Within the educational sector, AI has transitioned from a theoretical concept to an active agent of systemic change in schools, learning systems, and academic research institutions worldwide. This comprehensive review examines the multifaceted impact of AI on education through a structured analysis of empirical literature, implementation frameworks, and emerging challenges. The study synthesizes evidence regarding AI’s contributions to personalized learning, administrative efficiency, assessment systems, and accessibility for diverse learners. Simultaneously, it addresses critical challenges including algorithmic bias, privacy concerns, surveillance risks, and ethical implications of large-scale AI deployment in educational settings. Through systematic analysis, this research demonstrates that when implemented with deliberate safeguards and human oversight, AI possesses significant potential to enhance educational equity, effectiveness, and student-centered learning approaches. However, reali

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Challenges and Opportunities for Women in STEM: Higher Education Perspective
abstract: STEM courses significantly influence the country’s economic progress. It has been observed that girls outperform boys in STEM in schools, but do not pursue STEM careers. Hence, a wide gender gap in STEM education at higher levels and related careers can be observed. Therefore, a more thorough examination of the present issues and developments in STEM education and the field is required. This study attempts to provide a broader understanding of the gender gap in STEM. A quick overview of STEM and its influence on the nation’s economic development will be provided in the first section of the article. Then, there is a discussion about bridging the gender gap in STEM education and careers globally and in India in particular. Secondly, the paper will outline some reasons for low women’s enrolment in STEM. Finally, the paper will offer recommendations to enhance women’s enrolment in STEM majors, followed by a conclusion.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Available Infrastructural Facilities for the Education of the CWSN: Rajasthan State
abstract: Inclusion, a right of Children with Special Needs, has been identified as an appeal to educate students with special educational needs with normal children. In education, inclusion is a process that ensures quality education for all children from diverse groups by providing equal opportunities for them to participate in all aspects of school life. And for effective learning for all, the school’s infrastructure is a key foundation, as the objective of the available infrastructure in secondary school education is to enhance student enrolment and improve academic achievement. Though many government policies and programmes, as well as other NGOs, are making continuous efforts to accelerate the learning of CWSN in mainstream education, numerous challenges hinder their learning; among them, infrastructure is critical. Therefore, in the present paper, efforts have been made to identify the available infrastructure facilities for CWSN in schools to continue their education. For the study, a sample was taken from 35 secondary schools in Rajasthan. The researcher developed a questionnaire to collect data. For the present study, the sample was taken using systematic random sampling. The study

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Revitalizing Indian Knowledge Systems in Higher Education: Implementation, Challenges and Prospects under NEP 2020
abstract: The National Education Policy 2020 represents a transformative moment in Indian higher education by positioning the Indian Knowledge System (IKS) at the center of curriculum reform and institutional development. This research study examines the systematic integration of IKS into higher education institutions, analyzing historical evolution, implementation mechanisms, opportunities and challenges. Through mixed-methods research encompassing document analysis, institutional surveys and stakeholder interviews, the study evaluates the current state of IKS integration and proposes evidence-based strategies for successful implementation. Findings reveal significant progress in establishing institutional frameworks, yet identify persistent challenges in faculty capacity, resource allocation and attitudinal barriers. The research demonstrates that successful IKS integration requires systemic transformation beyond superficial additions, demanding collaborative effort among stakeholders, adequate resource commitment and balanced harmonization of traditional wisdom with contemporary educational imperatives. This study contributes to the discourse on knowledge decolonization and offers practic

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Inclusive Education Practices for Children with Special Needs: A Study of Government School Teachers’ Perceptions in Uttarakhand
abstract: Inclusive education aims to ensure equal learning opportunities for all children, including those with special needs (CWSN). Despite national policy commitments, actual classroom-level inclusion remains a challenge, especially in hilly states like Uttarakhand. This study explores the perceptions of government school teachers in Uttarakhand regarding inclusive education practices, the challenges they face, and the available support mechanisms. A mixed-methods approach was used involving 50 government school teachers across Almora and Dehradun districts. Findings reveal that while most teachers show a positive attitude towards inclusive education, significant gaps remain in training, resource availability, and infrastructure, especially in remote and mountainous regions. The study emphasizes the need for localized professional development programs, mobile resource support, and stronger community-school partnerships for effective inclusion.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Integrating SWAYAM-NPTEL in Higher Education: Students’ Awareness, Perceived Benefits and Adoption Barriers
abstract: The SWAYAM-NPTEL platform represents a transformative initiative in India’s digital education landscape. This study investigates students’ awareness, participation patterns, and perceived benefits of SWAYAM-NPTEL courses while identifying critical barriers to adoption across different institutional types. Using a mixed-methods approach, we surveyed 150 undergraduate and postgraduate students from three higher education institutions and conducted focus group discussions with 24 participants. Results reveal moderate awareness (60%) but low active participation (40%), with significant differences between technical and non-technical students. While 80% of enrolled students recognized the value of IIT/IISc faculty expertise and 72% appreciated learning flexibility, key barriers—including lack of institutional support (45%), poor connectivity (38%), and curriculum misalignment (35%)—hinder adoption. The study proposes an institutional integration framework emphasizing curricular alignment, faculty mentorship, and infrastructure investment to maximize SWAYAM-NPTEL’s educational potential.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Examining the Effect of Parenting Styles on the Adjustment of a Single Child
abstract: This study explores the effect of parenting style on the adjustment of a single child. It also provides a framework for examining the impact of parenting on the overall development of a single child. According to Baumrind’s theory, the family environment plays a very important role in the socialization of a single child. The first school of a child is the family, and the first teacher is the mother. Both have a pivotal role in the life of a single child. Parents’ support, guidance, rules, and values nurture the confidence level, social ability and self-esteem of a single child. A secure, healthy and positive relationship creates a strong bond between a single child and parent. It boosts the level of confidence in a single child for facing the real-life situation of society. Parenting style beautifully shapes the social world of a single child. It also develops a feeling of exploring the world and creates a sense of belongingness. Research proves that the authoritative parenting style is the most beneficial style for the social development of a single child. It also fosters a feeling of safety, and a single child feels independent with the supportive guidance of parents.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: The Transmission of Knowledge in Indian Classical Dance: Odissi’s Pedagogical Traditions and Contemporary Relevance
abstract: Indian classical dance, particularly Odissi, represents one of India’s most sophisticated systems of cultural knowledge and embodied education. This study examines Odissi as a multidimensional educational discipline integrating physical training, emotional development, intellectual cultivation, spiritual practice and cultural transmission. Drawing upon archaeological evidence, textual authorities, temple traditions and the living Guru-Shishya parampara, this study explores how Odissi fosters holistic human development through the study of bhava and rasa, rhythmic training, expressive movement and the absorption of mythology, scriptures and Indian philosophical thought. The paper traces Odissi’s evolution through centuries-old pedagogical systems -the Mahari tradition, Gotipua akhadas, traditional gurukulas and modern institutional frameworks -demonstrating its continuous relevance as an educational paradigm. Through qualitative analysis combining textual study, ethnographic observation and experiential documentation, this study illuminates how classical dance education enhances cognitive abilities, memory, concentration, discipline and emotional intelligence. journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Redefining ‘Indian’ Culture: Rituals as Markers of Identity
abstract: This paper will examine the role of religious rituals, especially those centred on marriage, in defining the identity of the Indian diaspora. There are variations among religions, communities, and even regions in how these rituals are observed. Individuals belonging to the same religion/community often observe similar occasions in small but significant ways. These are markers of identity in the homeland. The way these rituals are followed by the diaspora and the degree of variation/similarity in their practice are the focus of the paper. The paper will explore the anxiety of belonging that first-, second-, and third-generation diaspora feel through representations of relationships and marriages in popular media. The diaspora faces a double conundrum: even as it seeks to integrate into the nation in which it resides, it also seeks to retain as much of the homeland as possible. This creates tension among first-generation residents, which is amplified in the second generation of the Indian diaspora. The role of Bollywood in creating a homogenous view of India and its impact on the homogenization of rituals, especially wedding rituals, will also be explored here. This paper discusses t

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Assessing the impact of technology integration in education on career preparedness and industry alignment
abstract: Technology integration in Indian education, catalyzed by initiatives like the Digital India campaign and the National Education Policy 2020, is reshaping career readiness and industry alignment. Emphasizing digital literacy and skill development, it addresses the critical digital skills gap, particularly in fields like artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data analytics. Online platforms such as BYJU and Coursera democratize access to quality education, fostering inclusivity and enabling students from diverse backgrounds to pursue careers aligned with their aspirations. Furthermore, technology integration nurtures innovation and entrepreneurship among Indian students through initiatives like the Atal Tinkering Labs and Startup India. Fostering an entrepreneurial mindset and providing practical problem-solving experiences equips students with the skills needed to excel in a competitive global market. However, challenges such as the digital divide and the need for effective teacher training persist. Overcoming these hurdles requires collaborative efforts from policymakers, educators, and stakeholders to ensure equitable access to technology-enabled learning and enhance teac

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Research investigation on the psychological effects of procrastination on students in icse schools
abstract: Procrastination is a self-defeating pattern of behaviours; it may also be perceived as having a psychological benefit, particularly for perfectionists since it shields the person from shame, guilt, and fear of failing. Devoting energy to other chores such as organizing or cleaning instead of disagreeable labour helps procrastinators avoid feeling unproductive, even though they will eventually pay the price for it. Academic procrastination, which is classified as a domain-specific behaviour describes students' propensity to put off or postpone finishing assignments that have a set deadline such as writing an essay, doing their homework or preparing for an exam.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Scientific aptitude in indian secondary education: A comprehensive review and future directions
abstract: Scientific aptitude among secondary school pupils in India is a major source of worry for educators and policymakers. This thorough review seeks to offer an overview of available studies on scientific aptitude in Indian secondary schools, highlighting major topics, trends, and gaps in the literature. It draws on a wide range of research published in both national and international publications to synthesize data about the measurement, predictors, and effects of scientific ability among Indian secondary school students. Key subjects covered include the impact of gender, socio-economic position, and academic accomplishment on scientific aptitude and the function of pedagogical techniques, curriculum design, and educational policy in supporting its development. Furthermore, the analysis looks at the consequences of scientific aptitude for future academic and professional paths, emphasising the necessity of encouraging scientific literacy and critical thinking abilities among Indian youth. Based on the literature's findings, the study concludes by proposing prospective areas for future research and pedagogical interventions targeted at improving scientific aptitude in Indian secondary

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Digital transformation in education through iot: Embracing the future of learning
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has significantly reshaped the educational landscape, transitioning from conventional teaching methods to student-centric approaches. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) into the educational sector marks a transformative shift, blending traditional teaching methodologies with innovative technology-driven approaches. This paradigm shift emphasizes personalized learning pathways, real-time analytics, and efficient resource allocation, ultimately enhancing student engagement and learning outcomes. The transformative impact of IoT in education is multifaceted. One of its standout features is the ability to provide personalized learning pathways. With IoTenabled devices and systems, educators can gather real-time data on student performance, preferences, and progress. This data-driven approach allows for the customization of learning content and methodologies, catering to the unique learning styles and pace of each student. Despite its promising potential, the adoption of IoT in education presents challenges such as cost implications, ethical concerns, infrastructure limitations, and security risks. However, the benefits are substantial, includin

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Leveraging digital platforms for accessible education in schools: A blended learning approach
abstract: In the current era of digitalization, the process of incorporating digital technologies into the educational system to improve its quality and make it more inclusive, accessible, and economical is known as the ‘digital transformation of education’. As smartphone adoption and internet connectivity have increased quickly, digital education platforms have become essential resources for democratizing access to education. As mentioned in the NEP 2020, “The recent rise in epidemics and pandemics necessitates that we are ready with alternative modes of quality education whenever and wherever traditional and in-person modes of education are not possible. In this regard, the National Education Policy 2020 recognizes the importance of leveraging the advantages of technology while acknowledging its potential risks and dangers”. This paper explores various literature that focuses on the integration of digital platforms into traditional school education through a blended learning approach, with the goal of enhancing accessibility, inclusivity, quality and achievement in education. It studies the role of digital platforms in complementing classroom teaching and how blended learning can cater to

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: An introduction of inclusive education
abstract: Inclusive education includes all kids in the similar class. It denotes a genuine literacy opportunity for all students, rainy or not, in a traditional school context. In addition, all scholars learn together, and the primary prominence is on the learners' skills rather than impairments. In inclusive education, all learners participate inversely in curriculum and co-curricular conditioning. In an inclusive environment, children with special needs pay out the majority of their time with other children.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: An overview of kaushalam program to implement vocational education in Uttarakhand
abstract: Opportunities for vocational learning are essential for developing skills and increasing employability. The distinction between theoretical knowledge and actual skills encapsulates the significance of vocational development. In non-vocational studies, students frequently delve into a wide range of topics for hours. They spend a lot of time in the library and on computers performing research and producing papers that help students continue to expand their theoretical knowledge in a range of subjects. Thus, their class time is typically limited to a few hours per week. Even within their field of expertise, they frequently dedicate a substantial amount of time to study the theories, concepts and practices employed by other experts in the field. They have a lot less chance to implement these concepts. This paper focuses on how the School Education Department in Uttarakhand is implementing Vocational Education in their schools through an innovative program, “Kaushalam”.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Multitasking behaviour of college-going students concerning gender and stream of study
abstract: Multitasking is an element of human behaviour that demands an individual to simultaneously engage in two or more activities. For instance, texting or watching videos while walking, speaking to someone while watching television, writing/reading while listening to some songs, etc. Several studies revealed both advantages and disadvantages to multitasking. However, the present study's focus is slightly tilted towards the disadvantages. The paper aims to bring forth the adverse effect of multitasking behaviour among the general masses. It also studied the significant difference between male and female college-going students in multitasking behaviour. At the same time, the significant difference between college students with Arts and Science backgrounds of study was also measured. Descriptive research has been adopted to assess the suitability of the current work. Using the random sampling technique, a sample of 150 college-going students was drawn from the East Siang district of Arunachal Pradesh. Besides, for collecting appropriate data, an Inventory on Multitasking Behaviour (IMB) developed by Mariammal, C. & Meenakshi, R. in 2019 was applied. The process of administration of tools a

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Opportunities to implement content and language integrated learning (Clil) approach in indian technical higher education
abstract: Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) is an innovative educational approach emphasizing authenticity, active learning, cooperation and real-world language use (Ball et al., 2015; Uemura, 2017). CLIL is more relevant in higher education than in primary or secondary education, as certain criteria have to be met for its successful implementation (Ball et al., 2015). The criteria include learners’ L2 ability, exposure to L2 and Literacy and Cognitive Skills (CALP) (Ball et al., 2015). In addition, a plethora of research on CLIL has already been done at the primary and secondary levels. However, very little has been researched about the effectiveness of CLIL at the tertiary/higher education level, especially at technical higher education (Aguilar & Munoz, 2014; Uemura, 2017). This paper strives to identify the opportunities available in Indian technical higher education to implement the CLIL approach by examining the engineering subject teachers' willingness to collaborate with the language teacher to develop and implement a CLIL program. This research employs a cross-sectional survey research design. The data collection tool incorporated was a questionnaire with both open-end

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Attitudes of special education teachers in integrating ict for inclusive teaching of children with disabilities
abstract: This Study examines the attitudes of special education teachers towards the integration of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in inclusive classrooms of children with disabilities. Through a survey of 40 teachers from a teacher training institute. The Study aims to assess the influence of teachers' experience and ICT proficiency on their attitudes. The Study uncovers potential barriers and facilitators to ICT use. Results from this Study provide insights into enhancing ICT training programs, thus supporting the effectiveness of inclusive education strategies for children with disabilities.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Advancing education for a sustainable future: The role of teachers' soft skills, personality traits, and work motivation within Nep 2020 framework
abstract: Education for a Sustainable Future (ESF) plays a pivotal role in fostering environmental stewardship, social equity, and economic responsibility, particularly in the context of the global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). India's National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 emphasizes the holistic development of students, blending sustainability with experiential and value-based learning to prepare global citizens. This study explores the critical role of teachers' soft skills, personality traits, and work motivation in advancing ESF, proposing actionable strategies that align NEP 2020 with sustainable educational practices. The findings highlight that teachers' competencies significantly impact students' ethical reasoning, critical thinking, and eco-conscious behaviour, which is crucial for building sustainable communities.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Ecological knowledge of indigenous people: A guide to meet sustainable development goals (2030)
abstract: The human race worldwide is currently grappling with several interconnected issues, including gender inequality, poverty, hunger, health issues, educational disparities, climate change, and environmental degradation. The Millennium Development Goals (2015) and subsequently the Sustainable Development Goals (2030) were established by UN nations to address these issues comprehensively. These goals suggest various means to address the numerous interrelated concerns for the welfare of people and the environment. The authors in this paper aim to highlight the relevance of understanding, documenting, accepting and using indigenous knowledge as a means of achieving these set goals. It also presents a brief introduction to various indigenous communities and their contribution to ecology preservation. Additionally, this paper raises a concern of preserving this knowledge to meet the challenges and perils of the modern world. An effort to draw attention to the growing necessity of reviewing the understanding that indigenous people once possessed and practised is also made through this article. This paper makes a call for action to different stakeholders to advocate for including tribal persp

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Understanding technology acceptance in higher education: An application of the Utaut model
abstract: Driven by a belief in ICT's transformative power for education, this research utilizes UTAUT to analyze student perceptions and acceptance of technology in learning environments. While introducing ICT in higher education institutions like Amity University in Noida, Subharti University, Meerut, etc., fosters undeniable benefits, understanding and influencing user behaviour towards these new technologies is paramount for successful implementation. This paper delves into the UTAUT model, elucidating the critical determinants of user intention to adopt and utilize information systems, including performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions. We showcase real-world applications of UTAUT in diverse educational settings, highlighting its power in predicting and promoting technology acceptance. Furthermore, we present preliminary research conducted at Amity University, Noida, to gauge e-learning information systems and UGD repository usage through the UTAUT lens. This initial exploration paves the way for a comprehensive study focusing on student perceptions and acceptance of these ICT tools within our university context. In conclusion, embracing I

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Attitude towards the internet of students of higher education
abstract: Higher education in universities is the most imperative mechanism for development and change. There has been a paradigm shift in higher education from limited ‘teacher centered’ education to unlimited ‘learner-centered’ knowledge. ICT is frequently used in education for the following reasons: a laptop for each kid with characteristics including reduced power usage, an inexpensive operating system, and special mesh network and reprogramming features; less priced laptops have been created for usage in schools on an individual basis. In this paper, we will discuss about the Internet’s problems to us every second and how much impacted by artificial intelligence, which is the cause of that.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Study skills essential for quality learning of students at higher education level
abstract: In Fundamental principles of NEP 2020, it is clearly stated to emphasize focusing on intellectual comprehension as opposed to memorization and exam preparation, and also to motivate creative and critical thinking to develop logical decision-making and innovation. These learning abilities can be reached by disciplined study practices or we can say that appropriate study skills are essential for optimal learning achievements. This paper is an effort to explore various study skills and their importance in quality learning in higher education in this new knowledge society.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Beyond health benefits: Social and psychological factors influencing plant-based yogurt consumption - A theory of planned behavior approach
abstract: This study focuses on what influences Danes’ inclination to try plant-based yoghurt alternatives, using Ajzen’s Theory of Planned Behavior as a guiding framework. An online survey of 265 Danish consumers, recruited through convenience (snowball) sampling, investigated the connections between intentions to consume, attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, perceived impediments, and perceived sensory qualities. journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: An analysis of social competence of senior secondary student of Government and Private School
abstract: The idea of social competence is multifaceted and intricate, encompassing not only behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and social abilities but also the expectation and motivational sets necessary for effective social adaption. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the social competence of adolescents in the 13-15 age range. The idea of social competence is multifaceted and intricate, encompassing not only behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and social abilities but also the expectation and motivational sets necessary for effective social adaption. The sample was chosen at randomfrom Government and Private secondary school situated in district Ghaziabad of Uttar Pradesh. One hundred and twenty (120) adolescents were surveyed about their social competence. The data was gathered by random sampling. and analyzed, considering the goals and design of the research.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Shaping the future: Unveiling the dynamics of teacher education under India's National Education Policy 2020
abstract: This article focuses on the recommendations made by the National Education Policy 2020 regarding teacher education programmes and teacher education institutions. With attention on teacher education reform, the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in India represents a revolutionary vision for the education sector. The present abstract delves into significant issues that have surfaced from the application of NEP 2020 in the field of teacher education. A four-year Integrated Teacher Education Program (ITEP) is being introduced by the policy, with a focus on technological integration, professional standards, ongoing professional development, and a multidisciplinary approach. Although there is hope for these reforms, There are several of substantial issues that require to be addressed, including the require for infrastructure support, potential resistance to change, and regional inequities. To successfully achieve NEP 2020's objectives, it is also imperative to address difficulties related to bridging the digital gap, inadequate finance, and larger socioeconomic issues. This presentation emphasizes how critical it is to solve these issues in order to guarantee successful implementation

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: A comparative study of the impact of scientific attitude on rural and Urban School students
abstract: Our progressive society faces new problems every day. To resolve these problems, one should take the support of thinking, art, common sense, coordination, etc. Science education aims to help students lead a useful life in society. The scientific committee has to be reformed by the time it reaches the high school level. Otherwise, it becomes uninteresting, and the dullness of the science subject increases. The environment of one school to another affects the personality of the students. Therefore, a comparative study of the effect of scientific inactivity on students studying in rural and urban schools has been selected for the research work. So that students of rural and urban schools get extensive information about their personalities, their scientific attitudes can be developed, and strong personalities, conditions, and environments can be created for development. journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Inclusive education: Available infrastructural facilities for the inclusion of the CWSN in Haryana
abstract: Education is of immense importance for every child as they are the nation's future citizens. Education for All is a movement that recommends providing quality education for every child, and it is their entitlement to receive an education regardless of their strengths and weaknesses. In a similar vein, inclusive education settings serve to meet the educational needs of students with disabilities in a way that is easily accessible to them. This study set out to quantify the infrastructure resources accessible to CWSN. Eighty secondary and senior secondary schools in Haryana were included in the study. The researchers created a questionnaire that was used to gather data. Systematic random sampling has been employed to create a sample for the investigation. The study's conclusions demonstrated that while CWSN's architectural facilities were excellent, its physical facilities, teaching learning facilities, and facilities for independent living needed to be better for CWSN to include them in mainstream programs.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Engagement of information communication technology in classroom
abstract: Throughout human history, discoveries and inventions have been inventions. That has significantly changed social processes and structures. The Agricultural Revolution and the Industrial Revolution created agrarian and industrial societies, respectively. We are now in another such era caused by information and communication technology (ICT). As the creation, access, processing, and distribution of information becomes faster and easier, society shapes these processes so much that it is known as the information society. Participating in this society requires developing new skills and being aware of the ways in which these procedures impact equity and justice in society. It falls under the purview of education system to respond to this by bringing into school education an understanding of ICT, the effects of ICT and society, the possibilities of learning through ICT, and concurrently building skills in pupils who get ready for it. Functioning and sensitive in a society shaped by ICT. Knowledge is not new to men; communication has been called since man lived in caves. Information and communication technology is therefore as old as man himself before the invention of language, people had

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Sustainable development through green technology: Challenges and opportunities
abstract: Green technology is a strong instrument that can be beneficial to us to achieve sustainable development. Investing in green technology can create a more prosperous, healthier, and equitable future for all. In this article, author’s draws attention towards why green technology is relevant for us and what are its challenges and opportunities.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: A comparative study of lecture with chalk and talk and E-content presentation method for teaching english in secondary schools
abstract: In this study, the author wants to explore the variation between lecture method and e content presentation method in teaching learning. The sample has been taken from the secondary schools of Ghaziabad. This study was done in Ghaziabad. As we all know in today's modern times, the system of our education has the responsibility of presenting the knowledge in front of the students through technology and all over India is facing pressure to use e-learning and e-content to familiarize students with the knowledge they require in this modern time. E-content is a very powerful tool of education. The present research paper focuses on the evaluation of the effectiveness of e-content in teaching English among the students of Ghaziabad. The author used an experimental method in this study. In this modern time it will prove that our experimental method is more preferable than the chalk and talk method, which is reflected in this research. So, we can say that e-content is a very powerful tool to teach English to secondary students.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Gamification of education
abstract: Gamification is a method for enhancing the field of education by incorporating game mechanics into non-game settings. Although it is not a novel idea, research is still being done to encourage more companies, academic institutions, and libraries to use this approach in the future. It's not just that members of Generation Y, or millennials, are entering higher education and the workforce; regular smartphone use and gaming have also gained major acceptance. In this study, we will explore what Gamification is, give a general overview of its advantages and drawbacks, and discuss some of its applications.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Revolutionizing libraries: The role of AI and Nep 2020
abstract: The landscape of libraries is rapidly changing with technological advancement, and the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) have created an unprecedented opportunity for libraries to revolutionize their services. This paper explores the role of AI and NEP 2020 in transforming libraries and how they can improve library services in terms of personalized learning, content curation, digital preservation, resource optimization, and learning analytics. The paper provides an overview of AI and NEP 2020 and its importance for libraries. AI technologies are existing in libraries to automate tasks, provide personalized learning experiences, and optimize resource management. Furthermore, NEP 2020 provides a framework for the integration of technology in education, and libraries can play a key role in achieving the policy's goals through the implementation of AI technologies. journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Inclusive education and its perspective
abstract: The practice of enhancing student involvement in many cultures, curriculum, and communities at nearby mainstream schools is known as inclusive education. The process of lowering participation is, however, exclusive education. The concepts of participation, culture, curriculum, community, and locality must all be carefully considered in inclusive education. To put it differently, in inclusive environments, training is designed to convey to all kids, including the normal, endowed, and overlooked ones. In this article, inclusive education's meaning, historical background, objectives, barriers, etc. are discussed

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: THE world's potential response to Covid 19: Impact and preparations
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic is having a big influence on higher education as well; as a consequence, governments are sealing their borders and schools are going into lockdown. Despite the fact that higher education institutions moved quickly to replace in-person lectures with online learning, these closures had an effect on instruction and examinations, as well as the safety and legal standing of international students in the country in which they were studying. The current economic climate has brought into question the usefulness of a university education, which, in addition to providing academic material, also provides opportunities for socialisation and professional networking. This is possibly the most important aspect of the debate. For educational institutions to remain relevant and to make room for the development and enhancement of interactions between students, teachers, and others made possible by digitalization, the learning spaces that they provide will need to be reorganised.

journal_name: GYANODAYA: The Journal of Progressive Education
title: Students diversity in the classroom
abstract: The variety and inclusion of students in the sphere of education are the foundation of this document. Diversity is the practise of accepting students regardless of their gender, caste, creed, religion, or race. To uphold the principles of equality and diversity, one must not take any factors into account when enrolling students because each student comes from a unique social and ethical background. To be included, a kid must have an equal opportunity to access resources, education, and other opportunities. Nobody should ever be evaluated based on how much they have grown. Every kid has attributes that are distinctive and the talent to support them.
